mainTopic: Distancing damaging things from a neighbor's wall: launderers' ponds, plaster with lime, rocks versus sand, and seeds versus plowing
overview: The עמוד opens with the last line of an earlier discussion about bees and a neighbor's mustard plants. Next comes the משנה's rule about a launderers' pond. רב נחמן says the three טפחים applies only to a soaking pond (מחמצן), while a washing pond (נדיין) needs four אמות. This is first proven from a ברייתא, then retold as a contradiction that his distinction resolves. The גמרא then asks whether the משנה says 'and plasters with lime' or 'or plasters with lime'. Two proofs are tried, and each one is pushed aside. Next the גמרא compares our משנה's list of heat-producing materials with a list in מסכת שבת and asks why one mentions rocks and the other sand. After answers from רב יוסף and אביי are rejected, רבא explains that rocks scratch pots and dry sand does not harm walls, and it is defended against a ברייתא about damp sand. Finally the גמרא explains why the משנה lists seeds, a plow and water separately, and begins a new question about seeds that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why bees don't really harm the mustard
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of an earlier answer: the bees either won't find the part of the mustard plant that matters, or if they eat a leaf, it grows back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bees will not find it. And if they eat a leaf, it grows back.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that began just before this section. It explains why the mustard owner has no real complaint about the neighbor's bees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer covers both possibilities. Either the bees cannot reach the important part of the plant, or they only eat leaves, which grow back. Either way there is no lasting damage, so the bee owner does not have to move his bees.
steps.whatToRemember: No lasting damage means no obligation to move away. That closes the bees-and-mustard discussion.

phrases.english: [the bees] will not find it;
phrases.notes: This is the second half of a sentence that started just before this section, about bees eating the neighbor's mustard.

phrases.english: if [they eat] a leaf – it grows back.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ, אִי בְּטַרְפָּא – הָדַר פָּארֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer from the discussion before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual: the feared damage either does not happen or does not last.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mustard owner could force the bee owner to move his bees away because they eat the plants.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bees cause no lasting harm, so there is no claim.

steps.title: Soaking pond needs three handbreadths, washing pond needs four cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says the משנה's three טפחים applies only to a soaking pond. A washing pond needs four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Nor may one place a launderers' pond near a neighbor's wall. רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This was taught only about a soaking pond. A washing pond must be four אמות away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a launderers' pond. Then רב נחמן explains that the three-טפחים rule covers only one kind of pond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Launderers had two kinds of ponds. In a soaking pond (מחמצן), clothes just sit in the water. In a washing pond (נדיין), the clothes are actively beaten and splashed, which causes more water damage to a wall. So the washing pond needs a much bigger distance: four אמות instead of three טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: A soaking pond, where clothes sit in the water
A washing pond, where clothes are actively washed

steps.confusionAlert: Four אמות is far more than three טפחים. One אמה is about six טפחים, so this is a huge jump, not a small adjustment.

phrases.english: [The משנה says:] Nor a launderers' pond, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
They taught this only regarding a soaking pond,
but from a washing pond – four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three טפחים applies only to a soaking pond. A washing pond requires four אמות.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a launderers' pond needs four אמות. Since the משנה says three טפחים, the two sources must be talking about different ponds, just as רב נחמן said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: A launderers' pond needs four אמות. But our משנה says three טפחים! So we must learn from this that רב נחמן is right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רב נחמן. It uses the clash between the ברייתא and the משנה to prove his distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says four אמות and the משנה says three טפחים. Both cannot be about the same pond. The only way they fit together is רב נחמן's split: the משנה is about a soaking pond and the ברייתא is about a washing pond.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)?
Rather, must we not learn from this?

phrases.english: It is also taught this way [in a baraita]:
A launderers' pond – four cubits.
But we learned [in the mishna] three handbreadths!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו – שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב נַחְמָן.
phrases.english: Rather, is it not so? Learn from it that it is like Rav Naḥman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the statement in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's split between a soaking pond and a washing pond
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring four אמות for a launderers' pond, which clashes with the משנה unless it refers to a different pond

steps.title: Second version: the משנה and ברייתא contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: Some tell this exchange differently: they start by pointing out a contradiction between the משנה (three טפחים) and the ברייתא (four אמות).
steps.simpleTranslation: Some present it as a contradiction. We learned: A launderers' pond needs three טפחים. But a ברייתא teaches four אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the same discussion. This time it opens with a challenge, setting up רב נחמן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב נחמן spoke first and the ברייתא backed him up. In this version, the contradiction comes first and רב נחמן's distinction is the answer. The final law is the same; only the order of the argument changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Some present them as a contradiction

phrases.english: And some present them as a contradiction:
We learned: A launderers' pond – three handbreadths.
But it is taught [in a baraita]: four cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 2 and 3 as a contradiction instead of a proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires four אמות for the same launderers' pond, which is a direct conflict.

steps.title: רב נחמן resolves it with the two kinds of ponds
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה answers that the משנה is about a soaking pond and the ברייתא is about a washing pond.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: There is no difficulty. Here it is a soaking pond; there it is a washing pond.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the contradiction from the last step by splitting the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's three טפחים refers to a soaking pond. The ברייתא's four אמות refers to a washing pond. Each source is right about its own case, so there is no real conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source is about a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the law is the same: soaking pond, three טפחים; washing pond, four אמות.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
It is not difficult: here, from a soaking pond;
there, from a washing pond.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן מִן הַמַּחְמְצָן, כָּאן מִן הַנַּדְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each source speaks about a different kind of pond)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא disagree about the same pond.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a soaking pond and the ברייתא is about a washing pond.

steps.title: The משנה is read as saying 'soaking pond' outright
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב אויא teaches the משנה with the words 'soaking pond' written in, so the distinction is stated openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא son of רב אויא taught the משנה clearly: Unless he kept three טפחים between the edge of the soaking pond and the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא reads the משנה itself as saying 'soaking pond,' so the distinction does not have to be inferred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן had to explain that the משנה meant a soaking pond. In רב חייא's version the משנה says so directly. It also shows how the distance is measured: from the edge of the pond to the wall.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya, son of Rav Avya,
teaches it explicitly:
unless he distanced
from the rim of the soaking pond to the wall three handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts רב נחמן's distinction directly into the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's three-טפחים rule is stated explicitly about a soaking pond, measured from its rim to the wall.

steps.title: Does the משנה say 'and plaster' or 'or plaster'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact wording of the משנה: is plastering with lime required in addition to the distance, or can it replace the distance?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and plasters with lime. They asked: Did we learn 'and plasters with lime,' or perhaps we learned 'or plasters with lime'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה and raises a question about its exact wording. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה says 'and,' a person needs both the three-טפחים distance and the lime plaster. If it says 'or,' plastering is enough by itself instead of the distance. One small word changes the law.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a single letter in a משנה ('ו' versus 'או') can decide whether two protections are both required or whether either one is enough.

phrases.english: [The משנה says:] And plasters with lime.
A question was raised before them:
Did we learn 'and plasters with lime,'
or perhaps we learned 'or plasters with lime'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה requires both distance and plaster, or either one alone.

steps.title: It must be 'and plasters', or the cases would have been combined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues it is obvious that the משנה reads 'and plasters with lime'. If it read 'or', it would match the later list in the משנה (olive refuse and the rest), and the תנא would have taught them all together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that we learned 'and plasters with lime'. If you think we learned 'or plasters with lime', then the תנא should have combined the cases and taught them together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7 with a proof from how the משנה is arranged: the pit case must require both distance and plaster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later in the same משנה, a list of damaging items (olive refuse, manure, salt, and so on) says 'three טפחים or plaster with lime'. If the pit case followed the same rule, it should have been put into that list. Since it is taught separately, its rule must be different: both distance and plaster.

keyTerms.meaning: Plasters with lime (coats the wall so it does not leak)
If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
Let him combine them and teach them together

phrases.english: It is obvious that we learned "and plasters with lime,"
for if it would enter your mind
that we learned "or plasters with lime,"
if so, let him combine them and teach them together!
phrases.notes: A later list in the same משנה uses 'or plasters'. If this case had the same rule, it could have joined that list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer, backed by a proof, to the wording question raised in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה reads 'and plasters with lime', so both distance and plaster are required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The structure of the משנה: this case is not grouped with the later list that says 'or plasters with lime'.

steps.title: The cases may be separate because the damage is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The תנא may have split the cases because one clause deals with damage from moisture and the other with damage from heat, not because the rule is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the cases are separate because this kind of damage is not like that kind of damage. The first clause is about damage from moisture, and the last clause is about damage from heat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof in step 8 by giving another reason the תנא might have taught the cases separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 assumed the only reason to separate the cases is a different rule. Here the גמרא shows another possible reason: the type of damage is different (wetness versus heat). So the separation proves nothing, and the 'or' reading is possible again.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause / the last clause of a משנה

phrases.english: Perhaps it is because it is not similar,
this damage to that damage:
the first clause is damage from moisture,
the last clause is damage from heat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The 'and' reading may still be right, but it has not been proven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that separate teaching must mean a separate rule. The separation could instead be because the type of damage is different.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires plaster only for crumbly rock
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says that in crumbly rock, each neighbor distances his pit three טפחים and plasters with lime. This suggests that in normal rock, plaster is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, with rock that crumbles in the hands, this one digs his pit on his side and that one digs his pit on his side. Each one distances three טפחים and plasters with lime. The reason is that the rock crumbles. But if it does not crumble, plaster would not be needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to settle the question from step 7. The ברייתא seems to show that distance alone is normally enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה requires both distance and plaster only in the special case of soft, crumbly rock. The inference is that in ordinary ground, three טפחים alone is enough. That fits the reading 'or plasters with lime', not 'and'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rock that crumbles in the hands (very soft rock)
The reason (introduces an inference from a specific case)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Rock that crumbles in the hands:
this one digs his pit from here,
and that one digs his pit from there;

phrases.aramaic: זֶה מַרְחִיק שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים וְסָד בְּסִיד,
phrases.english: this one distances three handbreadths and plasters with lime,

phrases.aramaic: וָזֶה מַרְחִיק שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים וְסָד בְּסִיד.
phrases.english: and that one distances three handbreadths and plasters with lime.
The reason is that it crumbles in the hands;
but if it does not crumble in the hands, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 8 was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source to answer the question from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That plaster is normally not required together with distance, which supports the 'or plasters' reading.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה that requires plaster in the case of crumbly rock.

steps.title: Crumbly rock is mentioned only to rule out a bigger distance
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Plaster may be needed in normal rock too. The ברייתא mentions crumbly rock only to teach that, even there, three טפחים plus plaster is enough, and no extra distance is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even when the rock does not crumble: he must also plaster with lime. The crumbly case was needed because you might have thought that, since it crumbles, it needs more space. It teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the inference from step 10 by explaining why רבי יהודה chose to mention crumbly rock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 read 'crumbly rock' as the reason plaster is needed. The גמרא answers that the crumbly case was chosen for a different reason: to block the idea that soft rock needs a bigger distance. So plaster may be needed in every case, and the question from step 7 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach this case)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying plaster is needed only for crumbly rock. According to this answer, crumbly rock is mentioned to teach that it needs no extra distance.

phrases.english: The same is true

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא בָּא בְּיָדַיִם
phrases.english: that even though it does not crumble in the hands,
he also plasters with lime;
and the crumbling case was necessary for him,
since it would enter your mind to say:
since it crumbles in the hands,
let it require more space;
so it teaches us that it does not.
phrases.notes: Even soft rock needs only three טפחים plus plaster, nothing more.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא בָּא בְּיָדַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn from רבי יהודה's ברייתא in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the inference from the ברייתא is rejected. The question of 'and' versus 'or' stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed crumbly rock was mentioned to explain why plaster is needed. It may have been mentioned only to rule out a larger distance.

steps.title: Our משנה's list compared to the list in שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה about keeping heat-producing materials away from a neighbor's wall. It then cites a similar list from מסכת שבת about materials you may not use to wrap a pot before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה says: one must keep olive residue, manure, salt, rocks, and so on away from a neighbor's wall. We learned in another משנה: with what may one wrap a pot to keep it warm, and with what may one not? One may not wrap it in olive residue, manure, salt, lime, or sand, whether they are moist or dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by putting two lists side by side. This step is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists are about materials that give off heat. In our משנה the heat can damage a neighbor's wall. In שבת the heat would add warmth to the pot, which is not allowed. Since the subject is the same, the slight differences between the two lists stand out.

keyTerms.meaning: The solid residue left after pressing olives or other produce for oil
Wrapping or insulating a pot to keep it warm

phrases.english: One must distance the olive residue and the manure
and the salt and the rocks, etc.
We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת שבת, on 47b.

phrases.english: With what may one insulate, and with what may one not insulate?
phrases.notes: This means wrapping a pot of food before שבת to keep it warm.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין טוֹמְנִין לֹא בַּגֶּפֶת, וְלֹא בַּזֶּבֶל,
phrases.english: One may not insulate with olive residue, nor with manure,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בַּמֶּלַח, וְלֹא בַּסִּיד, וְלֹא בַּחוֹל –
phrases.english: nor with salt, nor with lime, nor with sand,
whether moist or dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה, after the discussion about plastering with lime ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה requires keeping heat-producing materials, including rocks, away from a wall. The שבת משנה forbids wrapping a pot in heat-producing materials, including sand.

steps.title: Why rocks here and sand there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה lists rocks and not sand, while the שבת משנה lists sand and not rocks.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different here, that it teaches rocks and does not teach sand? And what is different there, that it teaches sand and does not teach rocks?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the mismatch between the two lists and asks for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two lists are almost the same, yet each one has an item the other lacks. The גמרא wants to know whether there is a real reason for this or whether it is only a matter of how the lists were written.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason two cases are treated differently
Here / there: our משנה versus the other משנה

phrases.english: What is different here
that it teaches rocks and does not teach sand,
and what is different there
that it teaches sand and does not teach rocks?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּקָתָנֵי סְלָעִים וְלָא קָתָנֵי חוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the difference between the two lists quoted in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason each משנה left out the item that appears in the other

steps.title: רב יוסף: people don't wrap pots in rocks
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the שבת משנה leaves out rocks because people do not normally wrap pots in rocks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: because people do not usually insulate food with rocks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a practical reason why rocks are missing from the שבת list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His idea is that a משנה only lists things people actually do. Nobody wraps a pot in rocks, so the שבת משנה had no reason to mention them. His answer explains why rocks are missing from the שבת list.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: Because it is not the way of people
to insulate with rocks.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שבת משנה skips rocks because people do not normally wrap pots in them.

steps.title: אביי: people don't usually wrap pots in fancy wool either
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף with a ברייתא. It discusses wrapping pots in wool fleece and purple wool, even though people do not usually do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do people usually insulate with wool fleece and tabs of purple wool? Yet a ברייתא teaches: one may insulate with wool fleece, with combed wool, with tabs of purple wool, and with soft scraps, but one may not move them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer by showing that the תנאים do talk about unusual ways of wrapping a pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed the תנא only lists common practices. The ברייתא lists expensive wool and purple dyed wool, which are not normal wrapping materials. This shows a תנא may mention unusual cases, so 'nobody does it' is not a good reason to leave rocks out.

keyTerms.meaning: May not be moved on שבת (מוקצה)

steps.confusionAlert: The last line, 'one may not move them', is a side point about מוקצה. אביי's proof comes only from the fact that the ברייתא discusses wrapping in these unusual materials at all.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And is it the way of people

phrases.aramaic: לְהַטְמִין בְּגִיזֵּי צֶמֶר וּלְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל אַרְגָּמָן?!
phrases.english: to insulate with wool fleece and tabs of purple wool?!
As it is taught: One may insulate with wool fleece,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְצִיפֵּי צֶמֶר, וּבִלְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל אַרְגָּמָן, וּבְמוֹכִין,
phrases.english: with combed wool clumps, with tabs of purple wool, and with soft scraps,
but one may not move them!
phrases.notes: These materials are set aside for sale or for work, so they are מוקצה on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that rocks are skipped because people do not normally wrap pots in them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists unusual wrapping materials, so the תנאים do not limit themselves to common practice.

steps.title: אביי: each list hints at the other
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new answer. Each משנה mentions one item and expects us to apply it to the other. Rocks here also include sand, and sand there also includes rocks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: 'Its neighbor tells about it.' Here he taught rocks, and the same goes for sand. There he taught sand, and the same goes for rocks.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב יוסף's answer, אביי offers his own. The difference between the lists is only in the wording, not in the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, there is no real difference in law. Each משנה teaches part of the picture, and we fill in the rest from the other משנה, as the פסוק says, 'its neighbor tells about it'. So sand must also be kept away from a wall, and rocks also may not be used to wrap a pot.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Its neighbor tells about it': one source fills in what another left out
Rather: replaces the answer that was just rejected

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
"Its neighbor tells about it";
he taught rocks here,
and the same is true for sand;
he taught sand there,
and the same is true for rocks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי יַגִּיד עָלָיו רֵעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a new answer to step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation: the two lists complete each other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lists differ because of a real practical reason (רב יוסף)
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no difference in law; each משנה gives one example that teaches about the other

steps.title: רבא: then put the full list in one place
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי. If the תנא relies on one list to fill in the other, he should have put all the items in one list and only one item in the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If 'its neighbor tells about it', let him teach all of them in one place, and teach just one of them in the other place, and the same law would apply to the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer by showing it does not explain why the lists look the way they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא really wanted one list to fill in the other, why repeat almost the whole list twice and change only one item? It would make more sense to write the full list once and give one example in the other place. So אביי's method does not fit how the lists are actually written.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him teach all of them in one place

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If "its neighbor tells about it,"
let him teach all of them in one,
and let him teach one of them in the other,
and the same would be true for the others!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי יַגִּיד עָלָיו רֵעוֹ לִיתְנִינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that the two lists are written to complete each other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the method, the תנא would write the full list once and only one example elsewhere, not repeat nearly the whole list twice.

steps.title: רבא's own answer: rocks damage pots, sand doesn't damage walls
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains each omission on its own terms. Rocks are left out of the שבת משנה because they damage the pot. Sand is left out of our משנה because it does not harm a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: There, rocks are not listed because they scratch the pot. Here, sand is not listed because it keeps hot things hot and cold things cold.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected אביי's answer, רבא gives a fresh reason for each omission, based on how the materials actually work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף only said people don't wrap pots in rocks, with no reason given. רבא gives the reason: rocks scratch the pot, so they are not used for wrapping. Sand is skipped in our משנה because it does not heat up or cool a wall, so it causes no damage that would require distancing.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two places. 'There' (הָתָם) is the שבת משנה about wrapping pots. 'Here' (הָכָא) is our משנה about keeping things away from a neighbor's wall.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
There, this is the reason
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה in שבת about wrapping pots to keep food warm.

phrases.english: that it does not teach rocks:
because they scratch the pot.
Here, this is the reason
that it does not teach sand:
because it keeps hot things hot
and keeps cold things cold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's answer in step 17, רבא gives his own answer to the question from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separate practical reason for each omission
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two lists seemed to differ for no reason, or one list was supposed to fill in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each list leaves out its item for a real reason: rocks damage pots, and sand doesn't harm walls.

steps.title: A ברייתא does list sand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: רבי אושעיא's ברייתא does require keeping sand away from a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אושעיא taught sand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's claim that sand never harms a wall, by pointing to a ברייתא that lists sand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sand were harmless, no source would require distancing it. רבי אושעיא's ברייתא lists sand, so sand must sometimes cause damage.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught... (opens a challenge from a source)

phrases.english: But Rabbi Oshaya taught sand!
phrases.notes: He means sand is listed as something you must keep away from a neighbor's wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reason for leaving sand out of our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that sand does not harm a wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires distancing sand, so sand must be able to cause harm.

steps.title: The ברייתא means damp sand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא's ברייתא is about damp sand, which harms a wall because of its moisture.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about damp sand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא: dry sand is harmless, but the ברייתא is talking about wet sand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harm in the ברייתא comes from the water, not from the sand itself. So רבא's rule about plain sand still stands.

phrases.english: There, it is talking about damp sand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי אושעיא's ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say all sand is harmful.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only damp sand is harmful, because of its moisture.

steps.title: Then our משנה should list damp sand too
steps.stepSummary: If damp sand is harmful, our משנה should have listed sand and explained it as damp sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let our תנא also teach sand, and we will explain it as damp sand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: our משנה could have listed sand too, meaning damp sand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damp sand really is harmful, so it seems to belong in our משנה's list of things to keep away from a wall. Why did our תנא leave it out?

keyTerms.meaning: let us explain it as referring to (a specific case)

phrases.english: Let the tanna of our Mishnah also teach it,
and we will explain it as damp sand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer that damp sand is harmful and asks why our משנה left it out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Damp sand causes harm, so it should appear in our list.

steps.title: The water channel already covers dampness
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה already lists a water channel, which teaches that moisture is harmful. Damp sand would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It already taught a water channel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה already covered damage from moisture with the water channel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damp sand harms a wall only because of its water. The water channel already teaches that rule, so listing damp sand would just repeat it.

phrases.english: It already taught a water channel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why damp sand isn't listed in our משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Damp sand seemed to need its own mention.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water channel already teaches the rule about moisture.

steps.title: But the משנה lists two water cases anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה lists both a water channel and a launderer's pond, so it does repeat water cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say? Doesn't it teach a water channel, and also teach a launderer's pond?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer, since the משנה already lists more than one water case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the water channel were enough, why add the launderer's pond? The משנה clearly doesn't mind listing similar cases, so it could have listed damp sand too.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (opens a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ מִי לָא קָתָנֵי אַמַּת הַמַּיִם –
phrases.english: Is that to say? Doesn't it teach a water channel,
and also teach a launderers' pond?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ מִי לָא קָתָנֵי אַמַּת הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim that the water channel makes other water cases unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the water channel already covers damp sand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists a second water case anyway, so it could have listed damp sand as well.

steps.title: Both water cases are needed, each for its own reason
steps.stepSummary: The water channel and the launderers' pond each teach something new. Damp sand would add nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those are needed. If it taught only a water channel, we would say that is because water flows there all the time, but a launderers' pond, which is not always full, is not included. If it taught only a launderers' pond, we would say that is because its water sits still and soaks in, but a water channel is not included. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה lists two water cases. This is a צריכותא, showing that each case teaches something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A channel has water all the time but the water moves. A pond's water sits still but is not always there. Each has a reason to be harmful that the other lacks, so both must be listed. Damp sand has no new feature like that, so it is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed (each case teaches something new)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer stands. Rocks aren't used for wrapping because they damage pots, and dry sand doesn't harm walls. Damp sand is harmful, but the water cases already cover it. The two water cases are both needed because each teaches its own point.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the launderers' pond is just a repeat of the water channel. One has water all the time, the other has still water. That difference is why both are listed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic צריכותא: the גמרא shows that a משנה's similar cases are not extra words.

phrases.english: Those are needed;
for if it taught only a water channel,
that is because it is constant,
but a launderers' pond,
which is not constant, I would say no.
And if it taught only a launderers' pond,
that is because the water collects and stands still,
but a water channel, no;
so it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by showing both water cases are needed, which leaves the answer of step 22 in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The launderers' pond seemed to repeat the water channel, so damp sand could be added too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each water case adds a new point. Damp sand would add nothing, so it is left out.

steps.title: Why mention seeds if the plow rule already covers them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about seeds and a plow, then asks why seeds need their own mention. Planting needs plowing first, so the plow rule should already cover it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: One must keep seeds and a plow away from the wall, and so on. Seeds? Let us learn this from the plow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new part of the משנה and right away asks why seeds are listed separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you plow the ground before you plant seeds. So if the plow already has to be kept away, the seeds are kept away automatically. Listing seeds seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: One must keep at a distance
Let him learn it from (another rule)

phrases.aramaic: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַזְּרָעִים וְאֶת הַמַּחֲרֵישָׁה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The משנה said: One must distance seeds and the plow, etc.
Seeds? Let him derive it from the plow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the water cases to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's separate mention of seeds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seeds are always planted in plowed ground, so the plow rule already includes them.

steps.title: Seeds can be planted without plowing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means seeds scattered with a single throw of the hand, which needs no plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about planting with a single throw of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is a way to plant seeds with no plow at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone just tosses seeds onto the ground in one motion, no plowing happens. So the plow rule would not cover this, and the משנה must mention seeds on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: A single throw of the hand (scattering seeds without plowing)

phrases.english: With a single throw of the hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seeds always come with plowing, so they need no separate mention.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seeds can be planted by hand without plowing, so they need their own mention.

steps.title: Why mention the plow if the seed rule already covers it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the question: plowing is done to plant seeds, so the seed rule should already cover the plow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The plow? Let us learn it from the seeds!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the opposite question: why list the plow at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: People plow so that they can plant. If planting seeds is already forbidden near the wall, there seems to be no reason to plow there. So listing the plow seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him learn it (from something else)

phrases.english: The plow? Let him derive it from the seeds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 25, now aimed at the plow.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's separate mention of the plow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plowing is only done to plant seeds, so the seed rule already covers it.

steps.title: Plowing can be done for trees
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means plowing to prepare ground for trees, not for seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about someone who plows for trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that plowing is not always for seeds; sometimes it is for trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing around trees has nothing to do with planting seeds. So the seed rule would not cover it, and the plow needs its own mention.

phrases.english: With one who plows for trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plowing is always for seeds, so it is covered by the seed rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plowing for trees is a separate case, so the plow needs its own mention.

steps.title: Trees need water, so the water rule should cover it
steps.stepSummary: If the plowing is for trees, the trees need watering, and the משנה already forbids water near the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let us learn it from the water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer about trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trees need to be watered, usually with a water channel. The משנה already forbids a water channel near the wall. So the tree case seems covered by the water rule, and the plow again seems extra.

phrases.english: But let him derive it from the water!
phrases.notes: The water channel that the משנה already listed as harmful to the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the plow is for trees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trees need water channels, which the משנה already forbids, so the plow still adds nothing.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל, trees drink rainwater
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking about ארץ ישראל, where the land is watered by rain, so no water channel is needed for the trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is speaking about ארץ ישראל, as it is written: 'It drinks water from the rain of the heavens.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in ארץ ישראל trees are watered by rain, so there is no water channel to forbid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ארץ ישראל drinks rainwater. So the trees there do not need a water channel, and the water rule does not apply. That is why the plow must be listed on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: From the rain of the heavens

steps.whatToRemember: Seeds, plow, and water each get their own mention: seeds can be planted without plowing, plowing can be for trees, and trees in ארץ ישראל drink rain, not channel water.

phrases.english: The tanna is speaking about Eretz Yisrael,
as it is written: “It drinks water from the rain of the heavens.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting the place of the case, backed by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Trees always need water channels, so the water rule covers them.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ארץ ישראל trees drink rainwater, so the plow rule is needed on its own.

steps.title: Opening a new question about seeds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins asking whether this implies something about seeds; the question finishes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that seeds...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new question about seeds, and the rest of the sentence comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word למימרא signals that the גמרא wants to draw a conclusion from what was just said and check whether it holds up. We will see the full question in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say (introduces a conclusion to be tested)

phrases.english: Is this to say that seeds

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of questioning about seeds after the plow discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What follows from the משנה's rule about seeds (completed in the next part).
